Title: RTM to air Harimau Malaya matches live, PM urges Malaysians to show support
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Radio Televisyen Malaysia (RTM) will broadcast Malaysia's matches in the FIFA Asean Cup 2026 live, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar said the decision followed questions from the public on social media yesterday about whether the national team's matches would be shown live.
"Praise be to God, I want to share some good news. RTM will broadcast the Harimau Malaya matches live, starting with the match against Bangladesh tomorrow," he said in a Facebook post today.
He also urged Malaysians to rally behind the national team and support the players.
"Let's give our full support to the national team!" he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 40kph limit introduced at Federal Highway motorcycle crash site, lane resurfaced
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The motorcycle lane on the Federal Highway heading towards Klang, where several riders crashed at the same location, will be resurfaced and fitted with a 40kph speed sign.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the improvements would be carried out following initial action by the Public Works Department (PWD) at the site.
He said damaged sections of the road had been temporarily patched, while a "Kurangkan Laju" (Slow Down) sign had been installed as an immediate safety measure.
"Skid tests in dry and wet conditions were also conducted to verify the actual performance of the surface.
"Following this, improvement works, including milling and paving the road surface and installing a 40kph advisory speed sign, will be carried out," he said in a Facebook post today.
Nanta said preliminary information showed that the coloured surface on the motorcycle lane had been designed and applied as an anti-skid treatment in accordance with the specified work requirements.
However, it was drizzling at the time of the incidents and the road surface was reported to be slightly wet, with several motorcyclists crashing at the same location.
He said PWD had been instructed to conduct a comprehensive technical investigation without drawing any early conclusions on the cause of the incidents.
Among the aspects being examined are the surface's skid resistance when wet, the condition of the road surface, possible contamination by substances such as oil or diesel, and the quality of the work carried out.
The investigation will also consider other factors that may have contributed to the incidents.
"What is important is that we learn from this incident.
"If the investigation finds weaknesses in the materials, workmanship, design or maintenance, we will take appropriate corrective action," he said.
Nanta also expressed sympathy to the motorcyclists involved and stressed that the safety of road users who use the lane daily remained a priority.
A 42-second video went viral on social media yesterday showing several motorcycles lying on the Federal Highway motorcycle lane, with several riders seen by the roadside.
The video also showed the coloured lane appearing wet, while other motorcyclists slowed down when passing through the area.
The post claimed the incidents occurred during rain and that similar incidents had happened twice.
In August, PWD said the coloured surface at the Subang exit was a localised surface treatment implemented based on engineering considerations and with the approval of the relevant authorities.
It said the coloured surface was intended to mark areas with a higher risk of conflict, such as bends and exit lanes, while reminding motorcyclists to exercise greater caution.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Digital assets already contributing to economic activity, but potential remained uncertain
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is laying the foundations for broader economic activity through digital assets, although their full potential will depend on how the technology and ecosystem scale, says the Securities Commission (SC).
SC digital strategy and innovation executive director Dr Wong Huey Ching said digital assets were already contributing to economic activity, although their longer-term potential remained uncertain.
She said the presence of companies and firms operating in Malaysia and employing people in the digital asset space was encouraging from an economic growth perspective.
"I think there is economic activity. Whether or not it fully realises the potential is something that we don't know," she said.
Wong was responding to a question during a fireside chat at the Luno Institutional Digital Asset Conference 2026, themed "The Next Chapter: Malaysia's Evolving Digital Asset Regulatory Framework."
Wong said SC saw potential for digital assets and blockchain-based solutions to address issues in the capital market.
She said there were still many unknowns, including varying levels of familiarity with the technology and whether it could scale effectively.
She added that SC was closely monitoring how the technology could scale, citing evidence from selected markets while assessing how such applications could be applied in Malaysia.
Meanwhile, Luno Malaysia country manager Scarlett Chai said regulated digital asset trading should be viewed as part of the economic foundation needed for the ecosystem to develop.
She said trading value on regulated digital asset exchanges (DAXs) rose 23 per cent to RM17.14 billion in 2025, from RM13.93 billion in 2024.
"A well-regulated trading market lends confidence and liquidity for institutions to build and mature.
"At the end of the day, you don't get tokenised bonds or stablecoin settlement without a trusted market underpinning everything," she added.
Chai said regulatory developments were also strengthening the foundations of the digital asset ecosystem, including stronger client asset safeguards, financial stability requirements and management competency standards.
She said digital asset exchanges would also be brought formally into the Financial Markets Ombudsman Service under the SC's revised guidelines.
"In 2026 alone, we've seen multiple other tokenisation efforts across both TradFi (traditional finance) and digital asset ecosystems.
"The honest answer is that we are currently paving the foundations for greater, more robust economic activity, and the immediate two-to-three-year timeframe will demonstrate further potential.
"We would also start looking beyond trading volumes, and into tracking different indicators such as jobs created, institutional participation, or tokenised assets issued," she added.
Chai said Malaysia's regulatory approach also provided opportunities to attract companies building within the regulatory perimeter, including custody providers, tokenisation platforms, compliance and regulatory technology firms.
She said there was also an opportunity in Shariah-compliant digital finance, given Malaysia's established position in Islamic capital markets.
"The more of this infrastructure that's built and regulated locally, the more credible and productive the entire ecosystem becomes for investors, businesses, and the economy at-large," she said.
She noted that Malaysia's digital asset talent pipeline had also grown, although there remained tighter constraints for specialists in compliance and risk.
These specialists, she said, needed to understand both digital assets and Malaysian capital market regulations.
She said regulatory clarity and access to functioning sandboxes could be more valuable to serious digital asset companies than tax incentives alone.
"Malaysia doesn't need to compete on tax breaks alone. Regulatory clarity and functioning sandbox access, letting companies build and test without needing a full licence on day one, are worth more to serious builders.
"This is especially true for serious builders than a lower tax rate in a market with an uncertain rulebook.
"Continuing to invest in platforms for dialogue and closer university-industry alignment will do more for the long-term talent pipeline than incentives alone ever could," Chai added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia court reduces Gojek founder's sentence to 9 years in appeal hearing
Article:
JAKARTA: An Indonesian court has reduced the prison sentence of Gojek founder and former education minister Nadiem Makarim to 9 years from 10 years in an appeal hearing for a graft conviction relating to improper laptop procurement, judges said on Thursday.
Nadiem was sentenced to 10 years in prison in June after the court found him guilty of abusing his authority during the procurement of Google Chromebooks for schools in Indonesia that led to $125 million in state losses.
He filed an appeal on July 1 to the Jakarta high court.
One judge, Catur Iriantoro, said on Thursday that they did not approve Nadiem's appeal to dismiss all charges because the previous ruling was consistent with the facts established at trial, the evidence presented, and witness testimony.
The court also cut the amount of restitution Nadiem must pay from 809 billion rupiah ($45.23 million) to 548 billion rupiah, another judge, Subachran Hardi Mulyana, said.
After the hearing, Nadiem expressed his disappointment about the ruling and told reporters he would file another appeal to the Supreme Court.
"The victim now is not just me, but the credibility of the law enforcement system in Indonesia," he said.
Judges also upheld a previous ruling that said Makarim had adjusted the tender requirements to favour Chrome, which benefited Google and restricted competition.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Media Prima hosts PNB delegation at Balai Berita
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Media Prima Bhd today hosted a 10-member delegation from Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB) as part of a corporate visit aimed at strengthening engagement between the two organisations.
The delegation, led by PNB president and group chief executive Datuk Rizal Rickman Ramli, was received by Media Prima Bhd group managing director Datuk Rafiq Razali at Anjung Liku, Balai Berita Bangsar.
"One message is to continue efforts to spread positive messages to the people, and we hope PNB and Media Prima can work together to ensure both organisations achieve their goals," Rizal said.
[[nid:1540215]]
He said PNB's goal was to improve the financial well-being of Malaysians across generations.
The visit included tours of Media Prima Bhd facilities, including Media Prima Audio, News and Current Affairs and Wanita Hari Ini (WHI) Studio, Rev Media Group and the KLIK editorial floor.
[[nid:1540214]]
The delegation then attended a welcome session, followed by remarks from Rizal and a corporate presentation by Rafiq.
Among those present were Media Prima Content and TV Networks and Primeworks Studios chief executive officer Nini Yusof, Media Prima Audio chief executive officer Nazri Noran, and Media Prima News and Current Affairs Division group managing editor Jasbant Singh.

Title: Couple acquitted of trafficking 81.77g methamphetamine in Kelantan
Article:
KOTA BARU: A husband and wife were acquitted and discharged by the High Court here of trafficking 81.77g of methamphetamine in Bachok.
Judicial Commissioner Azhar Mokhtar made the ruling after finding that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against Syed Mohamad Haizat Syed Hassan, 32, and Nurul Syahira Zakaria, 30, at the end of the prosecution's case.
In his judgment, Azhar said DNA tests on the drug packets and a jacket used to wrap them found no link to either accused.
He said the accused's house could also be accessed by anyone through the main entrance or the kitchen.
"Next to the accused's house is a car wash where three workers often used the toilet at the house. They had previously been arrested but were released on police bail.
"Based on the evidence of the prosecution witnesses, there was no information linking the second accused, Nurul Syahira, to the drugs found.
"Therefore, the court acquits and discharges both accused without calling them to enter their defence," he said.
According to the charge, the accused were jointly charged with trafficking 81.77g of methamphetamine at a house in Batu 19, Kampung Badak, Bachok, at 11am on March 20, 2022.
They were charged under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, punishable under Section 39B(2) of the same Act, read with Section 34 of the Penal Code.
The provision carries the death penalty upon conviction and, if the death penalty is not imposed, imprisonment for life and whipping of not less than 15 strokes.
The prosecution was conducted by Deputy public prosecutor Nik Nur Adila Mat Zaidan.
Syed Mohamad Haizat was represented by lawyer Azrul Hashimi Mohammad, while Nurul Syahira was represented by lawyers Mohd Firdaus Zainal Abidin and Mohd Zubairi Salleh.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pas hits out at Penang Umno's push to strengthen PH-BN ties
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang Pas has hit out at state Umno's push to strengthen ties with Pakatan Harapan, saying the move puts political cooperation ahead of Malay-Muslim unity.
Penang Pas information chief Ustaz Muhammad Fawwaz Mohamad Jan said unity should remain the primary agenda for Malay-Muslims at both state and national levels.
He criticised state Umno leader Datuk Rashidi Zinol for advocating closer cooperation with PH despite DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng publicly calling for Umno's removal from the state administration.
Fawwaz said Umno holds only one executive councillor seat in Penang, leaving its position vulnerable to the discretion of PH and DAP.
Citing Negeri Sembilan, where BN has engaged in talks with Perikatan Nasional, he said political unity was achievable with sufficient political will.
"Why is Penang Umno choosing to complement the PH-DAP administration instead of building a stronger united front?" he asked.
While respecting Umno's political choice, Fawwaz said Pas remained open to dialogue.
"Ultimately, voters will evaluate which party genuinely works to safeguard the nation," he said.
On Tuesday, Rashidi, the sole BN representative in the state executive council, said cooperation between PH and BN in Penang must continue to be strengthened to ensure political stability and protect public interests.
He said cooperation within the state government had been constructive and effective.
He expressed hope that the spirit of cooperation and
understanding between PH and BN
in Penang would be preserved for the stability of the state and the well-being of its people.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nominee intervention halts consent judgment in Zetrix AI dividend dispute
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ongoing legal tangle over the dividend payout of Zetrix AI Bhd has escalated, with the two nominees of an unnamed substantial shareholder being officially granted permission by the High Court to intervene in a lawsuit between the substantial shareholder and the company's share registrar.
Zetrix AI announced the intervention today, which caused a proposed consent judgment directed by its board to the Share Registrar of the company to enter with the substantial shareholder be halted.
The latest development of the legal case has resulted in a computation mismatch in the designated dividend accounts, resulting in computation delays by the company in the remittance of the dividend payment to shareholders, said Zetrix AI.
Payment to affected shareholders would be made when the legal case is fully resolved, it said.
Notwithstanding that, the remittance of dividend to the unaffected shareholders is in progress and expected to be completed by Sept 28, said Zetrix AI.
The conflict centers around Zetrix AI's final single-tier dividend of 2.89 sen per share for the financial year ended Dec 31, 2025, which included an optional Dividend Reinvestment Plan (DRP).
The unnamed substantial shareholder, claimed as the beneficial owner over certain Central Depository System (CDS) accounts, alleged that the nominees operating these accounts failed to execute instructions to elect for new shares instead of a cash payout.
To prevent the cash disbursement, the substantial shareholder secured an ad-interim injunction from the Kuala Lumpur High Court, and the board of Zetrix AI subsequently directed its share registrar to enter into a consent judgment with the shareholder.
However, the legal landscape shifted when two nominees formally intervened in the legal action.
The High Court is scheduled to officially hear the intervention and review the ongoing legal action on Nov 11.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Smart seeks Budget 2027 boost to keep rescue gear ahead of the curve
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Continued investment in the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) is necessary to ensure it remains equipped with the latest search and rescue technology and equipment, says National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim.
He said Nadma hoped its allocation request under Budget 2027 would be approved to allow SMART to acquire new equipment in line with developments in search and rescue operations.
"Every year, during the budget screening process, we submit our application. I hope it will be approved so that next year we can make purchases, including the latest equipment.
"Just like the handphones we use today, technology and equipment for search and rescue operations are constantly evolving, requiring Smart to keep pace," he said at a press conference after the closing ceremony of Smart's International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (Insaraq) Heavy Urban Search and Rescue (Heavy Usar) recertification programme.
Meor Ismail said equipment such as drones and cutting tools was constantly evolving.
"We need to be ahead. For me, Smart is a special team, a specialised rescue team in the country. Therefore, its equipment must be the best," he said.
Smart recently retained its Heavy Usar recognition through the Insarag External Reclassification (IER) 2026 after undergoing a 36-hour field assessment covering 173 criteria, including command and control, medical response, technical search, logistics and the ability to conduct international operations.
He said the recognition was valid for five years, with Smart required to undergo another assessment in 2031 to ensure it continued to meet the prescribed standards.
In his speech earlier, Meor Ismail said Malaysia would continue investing in Usar capabilities, including equipment, training and inter-agency coordination, to strengthen the country's disaster preparedness and its ability to assist neighbouring countries and international partners.
"Reclassification is not the end. It is a new commitment to humanity. Malaysia will continue to invest in our urban search and rescue capabilities.
"We will continue to improve our equipment, training and coordination between agencies," he said.
He said Malaysia remained committed to strengthening disaster response capabilities and maintaining readiness to support international disaster response.
"We are ready not only to protect our own people, but also to support our neighbours and international partners when assistance is needed," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Family planning knowledge in the country remains low
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Knowledge of family planning methods among Malaysians remains low, with only 34 per cent of married couples using modern contraceptives.
The findings of the Study on Family Planning Practices in Malaysia also showed that misconceptions about contraceptive use had led some couples to be reluctant to use them.
National Population and Family Development Board chairman Datuk Seri Rohani Abdul Karim said the findings highlighted the need to strengthen literacy, access to and use of family planning services so that couples could make informed decisions regarding pregnancy based on their family's needs and financial capabilities.
"This study is important because it is evidence-based and shows that knowledge about contraceptive methods remains low. We thought the public already knew about this, but the study confirms otherwise," she told reporters after the launch of the report here today.
Rohani said the report also showed that the involvement of male partners in making family planning decisions was low, with most leaving the responsibility to their wives.
She added that the report identified high costs associated with family planning methods and subfertility treatments, as well as limited access to fertility treatment services.
"Social stigma against women experiencing subfertility issues persists. Often, when a couple does not conceive, the woman is blamed, whereas we need to consider the condition of both the husband and wife," she said.
Rohani said one in five cases in the study involved couples delaying seeking help due to embarrassment or the belief that they were 'imperfect'.
"If you have been married for one or two years and wish to have children but have not yet succeeded, please come to the board for check-ups and testing so that early intervention can be carried out," she said.
Regarding efforts to raise awareness among the approximately nine million youths, Rohani said the board would continue to intensify the Kafe@TEEN programme, as well as various educational and awareness initiatives related to family planning.
She said young people need to be provided with adequate information and support to help them make decisions regarding marriage, family formation, and childbearing, including how to manage the constraints of the cost of living.
According to her, the board hopes the report's findings will assist in strengthening family planning policies, programs, and service delivery. Additionally, the findings are intended to serve as a reference for policymakers, healthcare providers, academic institutions, professional bodies, and strategic partners in formulating more effective interventions.
Meanwhile, board director-general Datuk Abdul Shukur Abdullah said that the agency aims for 47,000 individuals to gain access to subfertility treatment, with 45,000 individuals having already gained such access as of September this year.
He noted that the board currently operates four subfertility treatment centres - located in Kuala Lumpur, Bertam, Johor, and Kuching - and that the intrauterine insemination (IUI) treatment success rate of 15 to 20 per cent falls within the international standard range.
The study is being conducted by Kumpulan Perunding Universiti Malaya (UPUM) Sdn Bhd from Aug 1, 2024, to Oct 31, 2025, with funding from the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) Malaysia.
– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man claims trial over alleged attack on 79-year-old aunt
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An unemployed man today pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court to voluntarily causing grievous hurt to his 79-year-old aunt.
Kok Jung Tze, 50, is accused of committing the offence at a house in Damansara Heights about 3pm on Jan 18.
The charge under Section 325 of the Penal Code carries a maximum seven-year jail term and a fine upon conviction. It was read together with Section 326A of the same code, which provides for enhanced punishment when the offence is committed against certain family members.
Kok entered his plea before Judge Noor Aini Yusof.
Deputy public prosecutor Mohamad Fadhly Mohd Zamry sought RM20,000 bail and conditions requiring Kok to refrain from harassing prosecution witnesses and surrender his passport until the case is disposed of.
Fadhly cited possible flight risk, noting that Kok had returned from Australia in April.
Lawyer Joshua Tay, representing Kok, sought lower bail, saying his client was unemployed, caring for his father and had cooperated with police during investigations.
"We object to the prosecution's request for my client to surrender his passport as there is no risk of him absconding.
"Although he was in Australia, he returned to Malaysia after being contacted by police and has cooperated with the investigation," he said.
After hearing submissions, Noor Aini granted Kok bail of RM18,000 with one local surety and ordered him not to harass prosecution witnesses.
The court fixed Oct 26 for mention.
Lawyer Ooi Hong Ming held a watching brief for the victim.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ismail calls for review of directive barring state exco from offices
Article:
SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has called for authorities to review the order barring state executive councillors (exco) from entering their offices at Wisma Negeri.
Ismail did not name the agency involved, but said the restriction was issued verbally without a written order.
"I was informed that there was a restriction or directive barring exco members from entering their respective offices.
"I was also informed that they were not only prohibited from entering their exco offices at Wisma Negeri, but were also barred from carrying out their duties as exco members," he said at a press conference today.
Ismail said he had urged the relevant authorities to immediately review the directive, including its basis and scope, considering the ongoing dispute and the need to ensure that public affairs and state administration were not disrupted.
"This request to review the restriction was made through proper channels, without preventing the authorities from carrying out their security responsibilities.
"I urge all parties to give the state government and the legal process room to resolve this dispute.
"The state government will continue to act with decorum, respect the institutions of the Negri Sembilan Royal Household and prioritise the interests of the people," he said.
Ismail said that, as menteri besar, he had never been consulted or advised on terminating any Negri Sembilan exco member under Article 38(5) of the state constitution.
"Therefore, I want to reiterate that the existing exco members remain legitimate and will continue to carry out their duties as usual.
"This is something I believe needs to be our focus today because the government must continue to function, state administration must continue, and the interests of the people must remain our priority," he said.
On Sept 21, media reports quoted Ismail as saying there was no need to submit a new list of
exco members
, as the existing line-up remained valid and would continue to carry out their duties as usual.
He said the position was based on legal interpretations and the limits of executive powers under the Constitution, particularly concerning the status and tenure of exco members.
The statement followed the immediate revocation of the
appointments
of state executive councillors after they allegedly breached the oath of office they took before the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan on Aug 7.
KW Negri Sembilan, state, Ismail Lasim,

Title: Sarawak's 17 new state seats unlikely to make next election — EC
Article:
KUCHING: The 17 proposed new Sarawak state seats are unlikely to be in place for the next state election, Election Commission (EC) chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said.
He said the review of the electoral boundaries for the seats would take longer than February 2027, when the term of the Sarawak government expires.
"The term of the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly expires in February 2027, so based on the process we need to go through, I expect we will not be able to use the new seats in the next state election," he told reporters after visiting the exhibition venue for the proposed Sarawak Electoral Boundary Review at the Kuching North City Hall here today.
In July, the Sarawak Legislative Assembly passed the State Legislative Assembly (Composition of Members) Bill 2025 to add 17 new seats, bringing the total number of seats from 82 to 99.
Meanwhile, Ramlan said the EC had received 18 objections to the proposed Sarawak Electoral Boundary Review so far, involving various issues including changes to polling district centres.
"There were also several objections concerning the names of certain state constituencies in Sarikei, Bintulu and Sibu.
"We will assess and examine these matters in greater detail later," he said. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Viral clip of foreign hawker's stall being vandalised sparks debate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A viral video showing local men confronting a foreign hawker and kicking down his stall has sparked an intense debate online.
In the 35-second clip, several men confront a foreigner preparing betel leaf (paan), demanding that he pack up immediately.
The confrontation turns aggressive when one man kicks a board structure, knocks over containers and throws stall items into a nearby trash bin.
The vendor complies without resisting.
The incident drew split reactions online.
While some supported the action to curb illegal foreign-run stalls, many condemned the violence and public vigilantism.
"I am soft-hearted. I feel sorry watching this. Maybe give him time to pack up and leave? He complied with your instructions and didn't fight back, right?" wrote Threads user j.e.b.a.t.8.5.
Echoing similar concerns, user tengkuazlan87 added: "He was indeed in the wrong, but kicking things like that isn't right. It's sad if his children had to see that."
Others emphasised that enforcement against unlicensed hawkers strictly belongs to municipal councils, not private citizens.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KTIP becomes first MIP-supported industrial park on the east coast
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MGB Bhd's Kertih Terengganu Industrial Park (KTIP) has officially secured Managed Industrial Park (MIP) support, becoming the first industrial park on Malaysia's East Coast to achieve this status.
Spanning about 687.9 hectares in Kertih, Terengganu, the development has been strategically master-planned to serve as a world-class, high-priority investment hub.
Backed by robust infrastructure, seamless connectivity and the advantage of 99-year land tenure, the park secured its planning approval in 2025, laying a solid foundation for its rollout and future growth.
The MIP support is far more than a badge of honour, MGB said in a statement.
It elevates KTIP to the highest tier of professionally managed industrial destinations, reinforcing its appeal to discerning investors targeting the East Coast corridor.
This validates MGB's rigorous, forward-thinking management framework - centred on world-class infrastructure, business competitiveness, environmental sustainability, and full operational readiness - cementing KTIP's status as a pivotal regional industrial hub.
To capitalise on this milestone, MGB has formalised a strategic partnership with the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) to champion KTIP to investors across Malaysia and globally.
Leveraging MIDA's extensive international network, the alliance will expand KTIP's visibility, streamline engagement with prospective partners, and deliver dedicated support throughout the investment journey.
The collaboration was celebrated at an officiation ceremony led by Tan Sri Lim Hock San, group executive chairman of MGB; Faizal Jalaludin, MIDA executive director of Investment Promotion; and Awasi Mohamad, chief executive officer (CEO) of TI Properties Sdn Bhd.
Joining them were MGB's group managing director, Datuk Wira Lim Hock Guan; executive director and CEO, Datuk Lim Lit Chek; executive director and deputy CEO, Lim Kim Hoe; and deputy CEOs Wong Tack Leong and Chew Wee Seong.
Hock San said securing MIP accreditation is a defining moment for KTIP.
He said it reflects MGB's commitment to developing a well-managed, competitive and investor-ready industrial destination on Malaysia's east coast.
"This recognition further strengthens KTIP's investment proposition and provides a strong foundation for us to introduce the industrial park to a wider investment community.
"Together with MIDA's extensive investment promotion network and international reach, we believe KTIP is well positioned to attract quality investments, create new business and employment opportunities, and contribute to the continued industrial and economic growth of Terengganu."
Faizal added that MIDA is proud to stand alongside MGB in elevating KTIP as a premier investment address.
"Through our investment promotion network, we look forward to promoting KTIP to potential investors and facilitating their investment enquiries and requirements," he said.
The MGB-MIDA alliance is set to accelerate KTIP's trajectory, amplifying its profile among domestic and international investors and driving quality investments that will shape Terengganu's industrial landscape for decades to come.
As Malaysia's East Coast emerges as a key growth frontier, KTIP leads the way - ready, accredited, and open for business.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Duo identified after dog dragged behind motorcycle
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Veterinary Services Department (DVS) has identified two men caught on video dragging a black dog behind a motorcycle in Batu Lancang, Jelutong.
The incident came to light after a passerby intervened and urged the men to stop, before independent rescuer David Yim lodged an
official report
with the department.
Following the report, Penang DVS director Dr Saira Banu Mohamed Rejab said officers acted immediately to locate the men and rescue the animal.
"The dog has been sent for a thorough medical examination and veterinary care.
"The matter is being investigated under Section 29(1) of the Animal Welfare Act 2015 (Act 772)," she said.
[[nid:1540159]]
The provision makes cruelty, abuse or severe neglect of animals a criminal offence, punishable by a fine of RM20,000 to RM100,000, imprisonment of up to three years, or both.
Dr Saira Banu said the department took all animal welfare complaints seriously and urged the public to avoid actions that could cause suffering or harm to animals.
She also advised the public against speculating on the case, saying this could compromise the ongoing investigation, and urged those with information to submit it through official channels.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AirBorneo signed four-year engine maintenance deal with P&W Canada
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: AirBorneo Airways Sdn Bhd has signed a four-year engine maintenance deal with Pratt & Whitney Canada for its ATR 72-500 fleet through 2030.
The airline said the maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) services will be done at P&W Canada's Singapore facility, which was opened in April this year.
AirBorneo chief executive officer Megat Ardian Aminuddin said the maintenance support in Singapore is close to its home-base in Malaysia, allowing the airline to get its aircraft back in service faster.
"That confidence gives us the operational certainty we need to consistently serve our customers on our intra-Borneo routes where reliable air transport is a vital link for remote communities," he said in a statement.
AirBorneo's current fleet consists of eight ATR 72-500 turboprop aircraft powered by PW127M engines.
Earlier, Megat Ardian told Business Times in an interview that AirBorneo is considering to phase out its older ATR aircraft as the Sarawak-owned carrier prepares to renew its turboprop fleet in the second half of 2027.
"We are still discussing that and there are a few options. Number one is to sell them outright," he said, adding that AirBorneo has received interest from operators and companies that could acquire the outgoing ATRs.
In February this year during the Singapore Airshow 2026 event, AirBorneo announced the acquisition of eight new ATR 600-series aircraft from turboprop manufacturer, ATR.
The order comprises five ATR 72-600s and three ATR 42-600s with purchase rights for four additional aircraft. Deliveries are scheduled between 2027 and 2029.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Wawasan questions RoS' timing in suspending PN ahead of Melaka polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) has questioned the timing of the Registrar of Societies' (RoS) decision to suspend Perikatan Nasional (PN), as the Melaka election looms.
In a statement today, Wawasan said it had been informed of two notices issued by RoS against PN, dated Sept 22 and 23.
The first was a notice under subsection 13(2) of the Societies Act 1966, allowing PN to respond to a complaint lodged by Bersatu.
The second was an order under subsection 13(2A) of the same Act to suspend PN's activities.
Wawasan questioned whether "hidden hands" were behind the notices, given their timing alongside the announcement of the dissolution of the Melaka legislative assembly.
The party claimed the action was politically motivated and aimed at preventing PN from contesting in the upcoming Melaka election.
Wawasan said it would continue working closely with other PN component parties to ensure preparations for the Melaka election proceeded as planned.
Previously, RoS clarified that the notice was not a decision to deregister PN, while the
suspension
took effect on Sept 23.
The department said the action was intended to safeguard the coalition's interests and prevent further breaches of its rules.
Meanwhile, PN secretary-general Datuk Seri
Takiyuddin Hassan
said the coalition disagreed with the basis of RoS' decision and was taking immediate legal steps to defend its position.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Schneider to launch €1.2 billion takeover bid for smart device firm Shelly
Article:
FRANCE: France's Schneider Electric said on Thursday it intended to launch a voluntary public takeover offer for Bulgarian smart-home device maker Shelly Group for €70 per share.
The all-cash offer values Shelly at about €1.2 billion (US$1.4 billion) and is expected to close by the first quarter of 2027, Schneider said in a statement.
The offer price represents a 27 per cent premium to Shelly's unaffected reference price as of July 28, and is 22 per cent above its current reference price.
Shelly's two founders, Dimitar Dimitrov and Svetlin Todorov, hold roughly 57 per cent of the share capital between them. Both have conditionally agreed to sell.
The deal would push Schneider deeper into the connected home market, where it competes with French rival Legrand, Sweden's Plejd and Switzerland's ABB.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Body found floating in pond off Jalan Pontian-Skudai
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: An unidentified man's body was found floating near the bank of a pond along Jalan Pontian-Skudai here last night.
Johor Fire and Rescue Department received a distress call at 7.26pm and deployed seven personnel from the Skudai station, who arrived seven minutes later.
The operation to retrieve the body was led by commander Inggai Bakau.
He said the body was found floating near the pond bank and no identification documents were found on the victim.
The body was handed over to the Kangkar Pulai police for further action.
The operation ended at 9.45pm.
Iskandar Puteri police have yet to issue further details on the victim. Investigations are ongoing.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China's fuel inventories hit over decade lows, raising concerns over comeback of export curbs
Article:
BEIJING: China's gasoline and diesel inventories have fallen to their lowest levels in more than a decade as exports surge and domestic demand recovers seasonally, according to GL Consulting.
Low stock levels appear to have raised Beijing's concerns, increasing the prospect of tighter export controls in October, according to Rystad Energy.
GL Consulting said it expects exports to fall in October as state refiners prioritise domestic energy security.
Commercial gasoline inventories have hit their lowest level since 2011, while diesel inventories have fallen to their lowest since 2015, according to data provided by GL Consulting, a consultancy owned by Mysteel, a leading commodity information provider.
China does not publicly disclose fuel inventory data, while GL Consulting's records date back to 2011.
The world's biggest crude oil importer has cut refinery throughput by seven per cent this year, as supply disruptions forced refiners to cut runs and Beijing imposed fuel export restrictions in mid-March.
However, China began easing the restrictions in mid-July, with exports rebounding to prewar levels in August, and they are expected to maintain their strong momentum in September.
The recovery has brought windfall profits for refiners and supported higher refinery runs.
China has yet to issue its October fuel export plan to refiners.
Some analysts have also lowered their estimates for China's fourth-quarter crude imports as Middle East supply disruptions intensify, and expect current refinery run rates to be unsustainable.
Energy Aspects has lowered its forecast for China's fourth-quarter crude imports to 9.2 million barrels per.
Rystad Energy has lowered its fourth-quarter refinery throughput forecast by 880,000 bpd from its previous estimate, to 13.9 million bpd.
"High crude costs are now forcing independent refiners to trim run rates. With state-owned refiners also entering their maintenance season, they cannot fully offset the production shortfall," said Ye Lin, vice president at Rystad Energy.
"The upshot is a sector with little room to manoeuvre. Tighter export restrictions would also mean forgoing attractive export margins, but China must safeguard domestic supply." — REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia reaffirmed as member of Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group
Article:
NEW YORK: Malaysia has been reaffirmed as a member of the Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group (CMAG), the body tasked with upholding Commonwealth values and principles.
The matter was raised during a courtesy call by Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan on Commonwealth secretary-general Shirley Botchwey on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly.
"The meeting discussed the Commonwealth's direction in addressing current challenges, including those relating to democratic principles, the rule of law and human rights.
"In this regard, Malaysia continues to be entrusted as a member of the Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group to defend Commonwealth values and principles.
"Malaysia has been a CMAG member since 2018," according to a readout of the courtesy call issued today.
The statement added that Mohamad and Botchwey also discussed preparations for the 28th Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM).
The Mohamad will represent Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim at the meeting.
"CHOGM 2026 will focus, among other things, on exploring trade and investment opportunities," the statement said.
Malaysia also welcomed the expansion of Commonwealth ties to include countries such as Bahrain, Brazil, Kuwait, Qatar and the UAE, all of which have been invited to CHOGM 2026 for the first time.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Westports puts sustainability into new facility: Deputy CEO
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Westports Holdings Bhd ensures it incorporates sustainability elements into the development of its new facility which involves stages of detailed study and assessment.
Deputy chief executive officer Linda Zain said the biggest challenge for the company to date is integrating electricity into the current operation.
The port's scale does not allow for these integrations to be made after development is complete.
Therefore, the company has been very thorough in adopting green aspects into the new facility.
"When we talk about a green port, it is not just about buying the technology, it's also about integrating the technology into the current system.
"The change management, acceptance, the policy, the standard operating procedures, and the trained people we need to ensure reliability and sustainability.
"So it's not just about building an infrastructure that is bigger, better, and more productive.
"But it's also to make sure that we incorporate the element of sustainability into the new facility," she told a panel discussion at the Green Ports 2026 International Conference held here today.
Linda said the company conducted a study in 2023 to analyse how much electricity is needed for the new facility.
The plan was then reviewed in 2024 to assess the carbon emission intensity based on cargo capacity.
"So then from there on, we planned what equipment would be required for the new facility.
"We are very concerned about waste management, recycling, and of course managing the construction activities to reduce carbon emission.
"As far as equipment is concerned for the
new port, the way forward is electrification," said Linda.
Westports is in the midst of expanding its facility by constructing eight new container terminals , CT10-CT17, to double the port's container handling capacity from 14 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs) to 28 million TEUs per year.
Linda said the company has completed the land reclamation for CT 10, CT11 and CT12 and the project is progressing on track.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Woman reported missing in Kuala Terengganu
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: A 23-year-old woman has been reported missing after leaving her home in Jalan Masjid Bukit Kandis, Kuala Nerus.
Kuala Terengganu district police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said police were looking for Nur Bahiyah Ahmad Shukri.
He said the woman was 153cm tall, had a dark complexion and straight, shoulder-length black hair.
"She weighs about 43kg and was wearing a black headscarf and a long-sleeved black blouse when she went missing on Aug 15.
"She was also wearing brown palazzo pants and slippers, carrying a grey handbag and a small grey teddy bear," he said in a statement.
Azli said police received a report on the woman's disappearance from her father at the Gong Badak police station on Sept 13.
"Initial investigations found that her father realised she was missing from home at 5.30pm on Aug 15.
"He tried contacting her but was unsuccessful and searched for her around the Kuala Terengganu bus station, but could not find her," he said.
Anyone with information on her whereabouts can contact investigating officer Inspector Rosfan Mohamed at 013-4895548.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] State secretary, legal adviser's positions must be resolved through due process - Negri Sembilan MB
Article:
SEREMBAN: Any issue concerning the positions of the Negri Sembilan state secretary and state legal adviser should be resolved through the appropriate legal and administrative processes.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Ismail Lasim said his government took seriously matters concerning administrative governance, accountability and the duty of every public servant to discharge their responsibilities professionally, impartially and in accordance with the law.
"The state constitution provides specific mechanisms concerning the appointment of key positions in the state administration.
"The government also takes note of the position of the relevant authorities on matters concerning the jurisdiction over the positions held by the officers concerned.
"As such, any questions regarding their positions should be resolved through the appropriate legal and administrative processes," he said in a statement today.
Ismail said, however, that the government's confidence in the administration, as well as issues concerning professionalism, impartiality and compliance with lawfully made government decisions, could not be set aside.
He said the principle of accountability in the public service must always be upheld.
"Public servants should not be seen as taking sides in political or institutional disputes to the extent that public confidence in the neutrality of the administration is undermined," he said.
He said the state government respected the federal government, the Attorney-General's Chambers and all institutions established under the Federal Constitution.
He said the same respect must be accorded to the state constitution, the state government elected by the people and the special position of Negri Sembilan's customary institutions.
"The state government reminds all parties, including any federal agencies or authorities, not to take any action that could be interpreted as taking over functions, exerting pressure or determining decisions on matters that, under law and custom, fall within the jurisdiction of Negri Sembilan.
"A healthy federal system requires the respective boundaries of power to be respected.
"Cooperation between the federal and state governments must be based on mutual respect, constitutional supremacy and the rule of law, rather than pressure or attempts by one side to override the jurisdiction of the other," he said.
On Tuesday, the
Negri Sembilan government suspended
state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and state legal adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal with immediate effect.
Ismail said the decision was made unanimously at a special meeting of the state executive council.
He said state financial officer Datuk Masri Razali would perform the duties of state secretary until a new state secretary was appointed by the Chief Secretary to the Government.
In response, Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said Zafir and Muzalmah
must continue performing their duties
as usual, maintaining that Ismail's decision to suspend them was invalid.
He said the two senior state government officers could not be prevented from entering their offices to perform their duties, as doing so would be unlawful.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: H&M's operating profit grows more than expected in third quarter
Article:
STOCKHOLM: Swedish fashion retailer H&M on Thursday reported a bigger than expected rise in June-August operating profit, as chief executive officer (CEO) Daniel Erver said his push to control costs and make sourcing more efficient was bearing fruit.
Operating profit in H&M's fiscal third quarter increased to 6.04 billion crowns (US$608.63 million) against a year-earlier 4.91 billion crowns and a mean forecast in an LSEG poll of analysts of 5.14 billion.
H&M meanwhile said it expected sales in September to rise by one per cent measured in local currencies.
Gross profit margin widened to 54.0 per cent in the third quarter, from 52.9 per cent last year, which included positive one-off effects from tariffs, H&M said. Analysts had expected a margin of 53.4 per cent.
Improvements within purchasing, cost control and operation efficiency contributed to a more profitable business, the CEO said in a statement.
"Although sales developed in a positive direction during the quarter, we see further potential to increase sales going forward," Erver said.
Sales increased one per cent in the quarter measured in local currencies. Analysts had expected sales to grow at a sluggish pace.
Erver said H&M is increasing the share of clothes it is buying in-season, as it tries to react faster to fashion trends, consumer tastes and increasingly unpredictable weather.
Erver became CEO in January 2024 with a mandate to improve profitability and strengthen the ​brand, but investors have been waiting for signs he can revive growth in the face of competition from Shein and Zara owner Inditex .
The billionaire family behind H&M is quietly ‌increasing its stake, fuelling speculation it could take the fast-fashion retailer private.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia-China ties built on trust, friendship, not just diplomacy, says Anwar
Article:
HANGZHOU: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has described Malaysia-China ties as having grown beyond ordinary diplomatic relations into a friendship built on trust and confidence.
Anwar said this foundation was among the reasons Malaysia placed great importance on its relationship with China and President Xi Jinping's leadership in development, governance and the pursuit of shared prosperity.
"Malaysia values the friendship forged with China, especially as both countries share many commonalities across a wide range of matters.
"This relationship goes beyond ordinary diplomatic ties. It is built on trust and confidence. We need partners who value friendship," he said.
He was responding to a welcoming address by Chinese Premier Li Qiang ahead of their bilateral meeting at the West Lake State Guesthouse here, during Anwar's three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou, which concludes today.
Also present were Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, Transport Minister Anthony Loke and Malaysian Ambassador to China Datuk Norman Muhamad.
Earlier, Anwar delivered the keynote address at the opening of the Fifth Global Digital Trade Expo, which was officially launched by Li.
Anwar acknowledged that Malaysia-China ties often came under scrutiny, including over Malaysia's position on its relationship with China and the South China Sea issue.
He said the government's position was rooted in mutual interests and the friendship built between the two countries.
"Premier Li Qiang, please accept with sincerity that we value this friendship and we see you honouring your commitments," he said.
Anwar said his presence in Hangzhou was not merely to discuss bilateral ties but also to exchange views with Li on more substantive matters.
Li said there was considerable scope for Malaysia and China to strengthen cooperation in digital trade, vocational skills, and science and technology, adding that this could make a fresh contribution to bilateral ties.
He also referred to Xi's state visit to Malaysia in April, which he said had ushered in a new chapter in China-Malaysia relations.
"China has always placed the development of its relationship with Malaysia as a priority in our neighbourhood diplomacy," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Australia's Firmus expects US$77mil first-half loss as it plans US$5bil IPO, sources say
Article:
SYDNEY: Australian data centre operator Firmus expects to lose US$77 million in the current half, according to two people familiar with a draft prospectus, as the firm prepares for a US$5 billion initial public offering (IPO) to fund growth.
Firmus, which is backed by investors including Blackstone and counts Nvidia, Meta and OpenAI as customers, is due to begin trading on the Australian Securities Exchange on Oct 22.
The IPO would be the second largest ever in Australia, ranked behind Telstra's US$10 billion listing in 1997, according to Dealogic data. Firmus could be valued at up to US$60 billion after the IPO, according to local media reports.
The share sale will test investor appetite for companies building infrastructure to meet demand for the computing power behind the artificial intelligence boom, analysts say.
Firmus expects to report a loss after tax of US$77 million for the first half of the financial year ending June 30, 2027, on a pro forma basis, the two people said, citing a draft prospectus circulated to prospective investors this week. The people declined to be identified because the information is confidential.
The document did not contain any further forecasts beyond the first half of the 2027 financial year, the people said. Firmus declined to comment.
The draft prospectus also described Firmus, founded in 2019, as historically loss-making, one of the people said.
Firmus' losses to date were attributed to the costs of developing and growing the business to be able to enter into substantial agreements with customers, the person said, with the proceeds of the IPO to be used to fund further capital spending.
The firm estimates its data centres, once developed, will make a combined US$5 billion in annual earnings within five years, a third person said. The company currently has two operational data centres in Australia and Singapore. Five more are under development, mostly in early stages, across the Asia-Pacific region.
The company will begin an institutional bookbuild on October 6, according to a term sheet reviewed by Reuters on Monday. The prospectus is due to be made public on October 8, the term sheet said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Digital assets enter institutional era after speculation, infrastructure: Luno chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The global digital asset industry has entered an era of institutionalisation, with tokenisation and stablecoins emerging as key drivers of its next phase, said cryptocurrency platform Luno.
Its chief executive officer James Lanigan said the digital asset industry had broadly moved through three eras: speculation, infrastructure and institutionalisation.
"The first era, the era of speculation, started in 2009, took about 2017. So this was all about Bitcoin, that was the only asset that existed initially.
"Until it moved on to the initial coin offering price. So this was all about volatility, it was also only about a retail audience, there was no institutional interest.
"It was only retail, and the price was really the only metric that mattered," he said at the Luno Institutional Digital Asset Conference 2026 today.
Lanigan said the industry then entered the infrastructure era from 2018 to 2022, when regulation, custody and institutional infrastructure developed.
"This is the era of regulated expenditure. So this is when policy was being created, it's where regulators were leaning in," he added.
Lanigan said the institutionalisation era began in 2023 and accelerated around January 2024 following approval of Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs).
This brought major financial institutions into the market, including BlackRock and Fidelity, while billions of dollars now flow globally on-chain daily, he said.
"So this is when the behemoth of the global financial industry led into your BlackRocks, your Fidelities and frankly, your technical skills.
"And now we have billions of dollars daily that are flowing around the world on-chain. You also have a huge acceleration in regulation as well. The US has been a major influencer on this," he added.
Lanigan said the institutionalisation of the market was already taking place, rather than being something expected to emerge over the coming years.
He said the market remained early in tokenisation, with about US$350 billion of tokenised real-world asset value currently tracked on-chain.
This compares with about US$200 billion in 2024, reflecting the rapid growth of assets being represented on blockchain networks, he said.
He said most tokenised assets remained in an early stage where the underlying financial product was essentially the same on-chain and off-chain.
"The product is exactly the same. But the reason why companies are doing this, and the killer use case at the moment, is distribution and access," he said.
Lanigan highlighted stablecoins as currently the largest component of the tokenised market, with about US$310 billion in value.
This represents around 90 per cent of all on-chain tokenised asset value, he said.
He said stablecoins were particularly important because they combined economic scale with a need for on-chain utility.
"It is the only asset that has both large economic scale and need for on-chain utility," he said.
However, Lanigan said the stablecoin market remained heavily concentrated in US dollar-denominated assets, with about 98 per cent of supply currently pegged to the US dollar.
"If you look at all of the foreign exchange and currency flow across the world today, only 50 per cent is US dollar denominated.
"So you've got this 48 per cent gap of growth that requires local currency denomination," he added.
Lanigan said this made the non-US dollar stablecoin opportunity a structural area of growth, with local-currency stablecoins expected to play a greater role.
He added that major payment networks were already moving into the sector, either by developing stablecoin infrastructure or acquiring companies in the space.
"Regulation has moved from what once was a threat to the industry to a completely inverted narrative today.
"So regulation has moved from a headwind to a structural tailwind. Institutions don't enter markets with legal ambiguity. They wait for clarity, and that in turn drives prosperity and growth in a market."
Against this global backdrop, Lanigan said Malaysia was not late to the digital asset industry, particularly in terms of its institutionalisation.
"Malaysia is not late for the party from a digital asset perspective, and certainly not from the institutionalisation of digital assets.
"It is early for everything that matters, the on-chain settlement, investment, liquidity, the non-US dollar payment rails leading into stablecoin and local stablecoin innovation," he added.
Lanigan said Malaysia also had institutions willing and able to start building in the space, supported by regulation focused on customer protection.
He said the combination of institutional participation, regulatory clarity and development of local-currency infrastructure would shape the next phase of digital asset development.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: SoftBank raising US$11.1bil in world's biggest high-yield corporate bond sale
Article:
TOKYO: Tech investor SoftBank Group is issuing US$11.1 billion in dollar- and euro-denominated bonds, set to be the largest high-yield corporate bond sale globally on record as it seeks to fund its mammoth bet on OpenAI.
The funding follows a one trillion yen (US$6.3 billion) bond issue aimed at retail investors this month, and is likely to prompt further scrutiny of SoftBank's finances, which could become vulnerable should market sentiment towards OpenAI and the artificial intelligence sector weaken significantly.
Under the leadership of Masayoshi Son, known for bold bets throughout his long career and now keen to make the Japanese conglomerate the dominant investor in AI, SoftBank has committed US$64.6 billion to ⁠OpenAI, of which it will own roughly 13 per cent by next week.
It is also acquiring ABB's robotics business for US$5.4 billion and DigitalBridge for US$3.1 billion.
The sheer size of its AI-related investments and the amount of money it has sought to fund them has led to higher yields to pay for SoftBank, which has long been a junk-bond issuer, as well as jumps in the cost of insuring its debt against default.
That said, the issuance is expected to go smoothly.
"I was positively surprised by the market appetite," said Satoru Aoyama, senior director at Fitch Ratings.
"Hyperscalers in the US have been raising debt but they have high credit ratings. Now AI-driven debt issuance has reached the high-yield market at scale," Aoyama said.
SoftBank is issuing dollar-denominated senior notes of US$1 billion at a 3-1/2-year term, US$4.5 billion at 5-1/2 years and US$4.5 billion at 7-1/2 years, a filing showed. The bonds pay interest rates of 8.625 per cent, 9.25 per cent and 9.75 per cent respectively.
It also issued two €500 million tranches of euro-denominated senior notes with terms of four and six years, yielding 7.125 per cent and 8 per cent.
By comparison, a US$7.3 billion SoftBank issuance in June 2021 of senior dollar- and euro-denominated bonds yielded between 2.125 per cent and 5.25 per cent.
FUNDING SCRAMBLE
A successful sale would mark the largest high-yield corporate bond issuance globally to date, surpassing French telecoms firm Numericable Group's US$10.9 billion issuance in 2014, LSEG data showed.
SoftBank has issued US$14.6 billion in high-yield bonds so far in 2026, making up 63.4 per cent of the Asia Pacific and Japan high-yield corporate bond market.
It has also sold off assets and taken out loans backed by its holdings in chip designer Arm and OpenAI to fund its commitments.
SoftBank's hopes for an influx of cash through the public listings of OpenAI and data centre development subsidiary SB Energy were dented in recent weeks as both delayed IPO plans that were set to launch as early as this month.
"Risks for SoftBank credit are material and have increased as concentration has increased and cash flow has come under material strain," CreditSights' head of telecom and media Mark Chapman wrote in a note.
SoftBank's holdings in Arm and OpenAI make up three-quarters of the group's asset value at current levels, he calculated.
The cost of insuring SoftBank's debt against default has shot up, with the five-year credit default swap spread exceeding 400 basis points this week, compared with around 280 basis points in June.
However, S&P Global Ratings' Makiko Yoshimura wrote in a note that Arm's strong share price performance has supported SoftBank's credit quality such that the delay to OpenAI's IPO does not have an immediate negative impact on SoftBank's creditworthiness.
CreditSights' Chapman sees the potential for a ratings upgrade in the intermediate term if OpenAI's IPO is "timely and successful."
SoftBank's shares were up 1.5 per cent on Thursday after Tokyo markets were closed from Monday to Wednesday this week for national holidays.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PM Anwar: China visit yields RM28b in potential investments across high‑tech sectors
Article:
HANGZHOU, Sept 24 — Malaysia has secured more than RM28 billion in potential investments following trade talks with major Chinese industry players, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The commitments were secured during a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou, which included a roundtable discussion with 21 companies and targeted meetings with five Chinese industrial giants.
The high-impact investments span several strategic sectors, including semiconductor manufacturing, artificial intelligence, robotics, electric vehicles, biotechnology, and advanced medical devices.
“The vast majority of these companies expressed their commitment to increasing investments due to their confidence in our stability and the policies we are currently implementing.
