The Prime Minister made the announcement following the launch of the Malaysia Pavilion at the 5th Global Digital Trade Expo at the Hangzhou Grand Convention and Exhibition Centre here today. — Bernama

Title: Emrail loses RM59m LRT3 bond suit, ordered to pay Kuwait Finance House RM39m
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — In a double courtroom defeat for rail contractor Emrail Sdn Bhd, the High Court has dismissed its RM59.1 million lawsuit against Kuwait Finance House (M) Bhd (KFH) and ordered the company alongside three personal guarantors to pay the bank RM39.09 million.
Justice Quay Chew Soon dismissed Emrail's claim over a disputed performance bond for the Light Rail Transit 3 (LRT3) development in its entirety and allowed KFH’s counterclaim in full, holding the contractor and its guarantors jointly and severally liable for the outstanding debt,
FMT
reported.
The three personal guarantors ordered to satisfy the judgment debt are prominent corporate figures Zaki Azmi, Hari Narayanan Govindasamy, and his son, Amrish.
The litigation turned on whether KFH was contractually bound to issue a performance bond conforming strictly to the template prescribed by MRCB George Kent Sdn Bhd (MRCBGK), the project delivery partner (PDP) for the LRT3 project.
“The central question underlying the plaintiffs’ claim is not what the employer wanted, but what the defendant (KFH) agreed to do,” Quay ruled in his judgment issued today.
The judge held that the underlying Islamic financing facility expressly stipulated that the Kafalah bank guarantee had to be in a form, and addressed to parties, acceptable to KFH. This contractual term gave KFH unfettered discretion to decide whether the wording and structure of the requested bond were acceptable.
The court further established that the specific performance bond template required by Emrail was never incorporated into the financing agreement with KFH.
Quay ruled that Emrail could not rely on its independent construction contract with MRCBGK to enforce obligations against KFH, which was not a party to that agreement.
“The plaintiffs have conflated Emrail’s contract with its employer/PDP and its financing contract with the defendant,” he said.
The court also rejected Emrail’s argument that KFH had acted negligently by failing to issue a compliant bond, ruling that a claimant cannot use the tort of negligence to extract a more favourable commercial bargain than what was negotiated under contract.
On Emrail’s claim that the lack of a compliant bond caused RM59.1 million in interim project payments to be withheld, the judge found that the contractor failed to establish causation. The court noted that Emrail offered no proof that MRCBGK would have certified or released the sums, observing that other LRT3 contractors faced industry-wide payment arrears, with Emrail itself eventually receiving around RM402.5 million under a subsequent contract for the rail project.
Ruling on KFH’s counterclaim, Quay held that the financing facility expired on Oct 31, 2021, leaving an outstanding debt of RM39,089,705.42 as of May 16, 2025.
The court ordered Emrail and the guarantors to settle the sum within one month, alongside post-judgment interest at 5 per cent per annum from the date of the decision until full settlement, and awarded KFH RM100,000 in legal costs.
Lawyers S. Shaarvin Raaj, A. Anusha, K. Ravvenneah, J. Jeyakrishna, and Iman Nur Alya represented Emrail and the guarantors.
Counsel Syed Faisal Al-Edros Syed Abdullah, Mohd Wafiy Azman, Choo Shi Jin, Nasbal Harun, Ahmad Iqbal Rohaizan, and Wardah Yunus acted for KFH.

Title: Air quality dips in Sarawak with nine areas unhealthy, Melaka also affected
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — A total of nine areas in Sarawak recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 4pm today, with the Serian District Police Headquarters (IPD) recording the highest reading at 200.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, other areas that recorded unhealthy readings were Kuching (188), Samarahan (179), Sri Aman (172), Bintulu (162), Sarikei (157), Sibu (156), Samalaju (155) and Kapit (133).
Meanwhile, 48 areas recorded moderate readings, including Batu Muda, Kuala Lumpur (75); Keningau, Sabah (60); Seberang Perai, Penang (53); and Kota Bharu, Kelantan (52). Another 11 areas recorded good readings.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 is moderate, 101 to 200 is unhealthy, 201 to 300 is very unhealthy, while 301 and above is hazardous. — Bernama

Title: MCMC backs police crackdown as Op Pedo nets 53 suspects, eight of them teens
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 24 — The collaboration between the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) continues to be strengthened to combat the misuse of network services for the purpose of online child sexual exploitation.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said MCMC, as the technical agency, would continue to play an important role in assisting PDRM, especially the D11 Division (Sexual, Women and Child Investigation) of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), in tracking down those who misuse network services and subsequently bringing them to justice.
“The MCMC’s role is to ensure that anyone who misuses network services can be traced, arrested and brought to justice, especially those who prey on children and women,” he told Bernama and RTM after attending the Communications Ministry’s ‘Jasamu Dikenang’ (Appreciation) ceremony here today.
Fahmi said the collaboration also involved technical and forensic aspects to assist PDRM investigations into online child sexual exploitation activities.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said on Sept 22 that eight teenagers, including a 13-year-old, were among 53 individuals arrested for suspected involvement in activities related to child sexual abuse material (CSAM) under Op Pedo Integrated 3.0 conducted recently.
The suspects were detained in simultaneous operations conducted from Sept 14 to 16 following intelligence gathered by the CID’s D11 unit with the MCMC, with police also detecting activities involving the production, distribution and sale of CSAM-related videos and animations through closed online groups, with the material being offered for between RM50 and RM60.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said the MCMC was also placing emphasis on the safety aspects of social media platforms through the legal framework related to online safety.
“Through the Online Safety Act, we are also emphasising to social media platforms the need to ensure that the environment or platform itself remains safe, especially for women and children, notably those below the age of 16 are not allowed to open social media accounts,” he said.
Regarding the appreciation ceremony, which honoured 157 retirees and soon-to-retire employees from the Communications Ministry, Fahmi said the experience and insights of retired civil servants should continu to be utilsed to help improve government services, especially in the field of communications.
“I pray that they will continue to find ways to share their views and contribute to ensuring the government’s efforts, especially in the communications, remain successful in the eyes of the people.
“If there is anything they wish to share with us for improvement, I am very open to receiving their feedback,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Sabah sees 10 million searches on Xiaohongshu as China tourism interest surges
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 24 — Sabah has recorded over 10 million searches on REDnote (Xiaohongshu), China’s leading social and lifestyle platform, signalling a massive surge in interest from Chinese travellers, said Datuk Jafry Ariffin
The Sabah minister of tourism, culture and environment disclosed the figures following his visit to the REDnote office in Shanghai yesterday, noting that the high search volume underscores Sabah’s strong visibility in the Chinese market.
“This is a very encouraging indication for Sabah. The interest is already there, and our focus now is to turn that interest into actual visits,” he said.
According to the minister, the platform’s users are most captivated by Sabah’s iconic sunsets, rugged mountains, pristine seas and fresh seafood.
Jafry believes this digital traction presents a prime opportunity to convert online exposure into physical arrivals as the state builds momentum for Visit Sabah 2027.
“We want more Chinese travellers to experience Sabah for themselves, from our spectacular sunsets and Mount Kinabalu to our islands, fresh seafood, wildlife and diverse cultures,” he added.
The minister said that digital ecosystems like REDnote are now pivotal in shaping travel decisions, especially for younger, independent travellers who shun traditional tour packages in favour of peer recommendations.
“China remains an important tourism market for Sabah. As we strengthen air connectivity, our destination marketing must also reach travellers through the platforms they use to discover and plan their holidays,” he said.
The trip to Shanghai is part of a broader strategic engagement in China to tighten industry partnerships and improve market access, ensuring Sabah remains a top-of-mind destination for the region.

Title: Masidi confident Putrajaya will secure Sabah borders amid Balabac Strait concerns
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 24 — Sabah Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun is confident the federal government will safeguard the state's borders in the Balabac Strait, despite concerns surrounding a US-backed Philippine military facility in the region.
Speaking to reporters after the Sabah Carbon Forum today, Masidi said that border security falls under the jurisdiction of Putrajaya.
“It’s under their authority. So, definitely, I’m very sure that our government has done all that is necessary and reasonable to make sure that our borders are well-guarded,” he said.
When asked if Sabah would see additional security reinforcements, Masidi replied, “All I can say is that I don’t think they will allow Sabah to go undefended.”
The minister urged the public to remain objective, warning against statements that could spark unnecessary speculation. He stressed the need for a measured approach to the geopolitical development.
“I don’t think we should emotionalise the issue because there are a lot of issues that are related to that. I think the most important thing is that Sabah is not in any way exposing itself to security breaches just because somebody is building a huge facility.
“We should look at it with a reasonable and cool head. We don’t want to issue a statement that will somewhat lead to a lot of speculation,” he added.
The concerns stem from the upgrade of a Philippine military facility on Balabac island in southern Palawan, situated near the Balabac Strait that separates the Philippines from Sabah. Under the Enhanced Defence Cooperation Agreement, the US is supporting the development, which includes a 3km airstrip.
This expansion has heightened security sensitivities in Malaysia, particularly given the Philippines’ longstanding claim over Sabah, a claim that Kuala Lumpur firmly rejects.
Regarding a meeting held on September 11, Masidi declined to disclose specific details, noting only that the discussions covered various matters in the best interest of Sabah and the nation.

Title: Police announce staged KL diversions as Sunday Coway Run shuts 34 roads
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — Thirty-four roads around the capital will be subject to road closures and traffic diversions in stages on Sunday (Sept 27) in conjunction with the Coway Run 2026 at the Merdeka Stadium here.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department deputy chief Supt Suffian Abdullah said the closures and diversions would begin as early as 3.30am on Sunday and the roads would be reopened in stages after the conclusion of the event, which is expected to attract about 10,000 participants.
“The roads involved are Jalan Stadium, Jalan Maharajalela, Jalan Dewan Bahasa, Jalan Bukit Petaling, Jalan Bellamy, Jalan Hang Tuah, Jalan Hang Jebat, Jalan Sultan Ismail, Jalan Raja Chulan, Jalan Conlay and Jalan Kia Peng.
“Also involved are Jalan Perak, Jalan P. Ramlee, Jalan Ampang, Jalan Raja Laut, Jalan Putra, Jalan Tun Ismail, Jalan Tunku, Jalan Langgak Tunku, Jalan Pinggiran Tunku, Jalan Girdle, Jalan Bukit Tunku and Jalan Sultan Salahuddin,” he said in a statement today.
He said that other roads that would also be closed were Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar, Jalan Persiaran Sultan Salahuddin, Jalan Parlimen, Jalan Dato Onn, Bulatan Dato Onn, Jalan Kinabalu, Jalan Tun Perak, Jalan Pudu, Jalan Sultan, Jalan Petaling and Bulatan Merdeka.
Suffian said the Coway Run comprised three main categories: the 30-kilometre (km) run starting at 4am; the 10km run starting at 5.15am; and the 5km Fun Run at 7am.
As such, he advised the public to avoid using the affected roads throughout the event, plan their journeys in advance and use alternative routes, as well as opt for public transport to reduce traffic congestion.
“Members of the public are also advised to comply with instructions from police and traffic personnel on duty at the locations to ensure safety and smooth traffic flow, as well as to practise responsible driving and remain patient throughout the road closures,” he added.
For any enquiries or further information regarding the programme and the affected routes, the public can contact the Tun H.S. Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or any nearby police station. — Bernama

Title: Father, teenage son held over Kuala Kangsar murder of woman with disabilities
Article:
IPOH, Sept 24 — A father and son have been remanded for seven and two days respectively, starting today, to assist in the investigation of a murder case involving a woman with disabilities (PwD) in Kampung Cheh Kati, Kuala Kangsar, yesterday.
The remand orders for the two males, aged 15 and 44, were issued by Magistrate Azlin Zeti Zainal Abidin at the Kuala Kangsar Magistrate’s Court here, following an application by the police to investigate the case under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
Yesterday, the media reported that a 49-year-old woman was found dead, lying in a pool of blood in the living room of her home in the village.
Kuala Kangsar district police chief ACP Heisham Harun said the police received a report regarding the incident at 2.38pm after family members discovered the victim lying face down and unconscious.
A woman was found dead in the living room of a house in Kampung Cheh Kati, Kuala Kangsar on September 23, 2026. — Bernama pic
According to him, preliminary investigations suggest the incident stemmed from a misunderstanding between the victim and the suspects while police also recovered a knife believed to have been used in the incident. — Bernama

Title: ‘Income first’: Economy Minister Akmal says Budget 2027 must deliver better wages for Malaysians
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 24 — Income and wages must remain a priority in the planning of Budget 2027, alongside efforts to strengthen the capabilities of local companies in high-growth, high-value (HGHV) industries.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said this was necessary to ensure that gains in productivity and Malaysia’s position in the supply chain translate into better job opportunities and more meaningful wages.
“That is why we believe the time has come for discussions on income and wages to remain a priority.
“As we plan Budget 2027, the issue of income must also go hand in hand with the capabilities of companies,” he told reporters after the ‘KL20@Penang 2026: Silicon Surge’ programme at the Penang Waterfront Convention Centre (PWCC).
Akmal said the allocation to Penang for the development of the National Automation, Testing and Equipment (ATE) Campus in Batu Kawan was also part of the government’s efforts to strengthen local companies’ capabilities, thereby creating better job opportunities and more meaningful wages for Malaysians.
He said the federal government had allocated RM25 million under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) for the construction of the campus, aimed at strengthening the state’s semiconductor ecosystem.
Meanwhile, he said persistently high oil prices and an uncertain outlook should also be taken into account in Budget 2027 to ensure the country’s development and the people’s economic well-being remain protected.
“In terms of the announcements or the Budget to be tabled soon, I expect these to be among the issues that the Finance Minister will focus on, so that despite oil prices remaining high and the outlook being uncertain, the country can continue planning for development and the people’s well-being,” he said.
Meanwhile, Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state government would provide land in Batu Kawan for the development of the ATE campus.
He said the initiative followed the state’s efforts to strengthen the chip design sector through Penang Silicon Design @ 5KM+, which was launched two years ago.
He said that, in addition to the ATE Campus, Penang had established a RM50 million technology fund as an initial measure to help start-ups and companies seeking to scale up gain access to capital.
“We hope this fund will grow with the participation of parties beyond Penang, creating a fund that start-ups and companies in Penang and across Malaysia can access for the capital they need to move to the next stage,” he said.
Chow said the ATE campus would serve as a platform for talent development, technology qualification and joint development, testing and deployment of Malaysian-made ATE solutions. — Bernama

Title: Hajiji: Sabah setting high standards to protect carbon credit reputation
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 24 — Sabah will not permit unvetted projects or speculative trading to undermine its emerging carbon market, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Panglima Hajiji Noor said today, insisting that strong regulatory standards are vital to secure long-term investor confidence.
Hajiji warned that poorly structured initiatives, exaggerated climate claims, undervalued natural resources, and the exclusion of native indigenous communities would severely damage the credibility of Sabah’s carbon credits on the global stage.
“It is therefore in Sabah’s commercial interest to uphold the highest standards of environmental, social, financial, and governance integrity. Buyers will demand full transparency. We will not allow unvetted projects to be rushed to market or traded on speculation.
“Through strong regulatory discipline, we will protect Sabah’s reputation and brand,” he said.
His speech was delivered by Deputy Chief Minister II and State Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun during the Sabah Carbon Market Forum here today.
Hajiji highlighted that the forthcoming Sabah Climate Change and Carbon Governance Enactment 2025 will provide legal certainty by officially recognising the state government’s ownership of carbon rights, subject to statutory provisions.
The legislation will also establish clear operating rules for carbon-related activities, ranging from project approvals to credit trading.
While no enforcement date has been set, Hajiji noted that the framework will provide investors with a streamlined, coordinated regulatory gateway for project licensing and carbon registry entries.
Under the enactment, the newly established Sabah Climate Change Action Council will steer state climate policy, draft the state carbon budget for cabinet approval and gazettement, and harmonize inter-agency cooperation between state and federal authorities.
The council will be supported operationally and technically by a dedicated Climate Registry and Inventory Centre.
Acknowledging that high upfront development costs pose a significant hurdle to early-stage carbon projects, Hajiji called on the banking and investment sectors to step forward with innovative capital solutions.
“We therefore challenge the financial sector to develop or co-develop practical financing frameworks that can bridge this gap,” he said, directing his appeal to major market players including CIMB Bank Berhad, Bursa Malaysia, and institutional investors.
Hajiji stressed that Sabah must balance project credibility, commercial demand, and structured financing to ensure that nature conservation translates into sustainable economic returns.
He added that the state is actively pursuing a diversified portfolio of carbon assets, targeting high-potential sectors including the blue economy, sustainable agriculture, renewable energy, green technology, and carbon capture and storage (CCS).
Citing tangible progress, Hajiji cited the Kuamut Rainforest Conservation Project, which encompasses approximately 83,381 hectares of lowland and hill dipterocarp forests, as a premier example of Sabah’s potential. The project is projected to generate average emissions reductions of over 800,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent annually.

Title: Penang DVS probes case of dog allegedly dragged by motorcycle in Batu Lancang
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 24 — The Penang Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) is investigating an incident involving two men who allegedly dragged a dog using a motorcycle in the Batu Lancang area here yesterday.
Penang DVS director Dr Saira Banu Mohamed Rejab, when contacted, confirmed that it had received a report regarding the incident.
“The Penang DVS is carrying out further investigations into the incident,” she said.
Meanwhile, animal rescuer David Yim said a woman who witnessed the incident had confronted the two men and asked them to stop, but they allegedly continued dragging the dog before leaving the scene.
He said the woman later lodged a report with the DVS, and also handed over photographs and videos believed to have captured the incident to the authorities.
“The black dog is believed to have suffered serious injuries and was left at the scene,” he said.
He hopes that the authorities will conduct a thorough investigation and take appropriate action if there were elements of animal cruelty involved. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB coy over coerced signing allegation, claims ‘overtaken by events’
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 24 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim dodged questions today regarding his police report over claims he was coerced into signing a proclamation on the position of Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, claiming the matter has been “overtaken by events”.
Asked by reporters for an update on the investigation during a press conference here, Ismail declined to elaborate further on the status of his report.
“Oh, that was a long time ago, overtaken by events. I have no comment,” he said.
“There is nothing more. It has been overtaken by events,” he added.
Ismail had previously confirmed that he signed the controversial proclamation regarding Tuanku Muhriz’s throne, but asserted that he had done so under duress and against his will.
He subsequently lodged a formal police report on September 8 to trigger an official investigation into the alleged coercion.
On September 15, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail confirmed that police had received two separate reports regarding the alleged forced signing and were in the process of classifying the case to establish the proper scope and direction of the investigation.

Title: Only RM6.7m recovered from RM2.97b scams, Lim Guan Eng demands urgent action
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Sept 24 — Lim Guan Eng today urged Bank Negara to spearhead a “whole of government” crackdown on digital fraud, cyber theft and scams, warning that billions of ringgit in life savings are at risk.
The Bagan MP said elected representatives nationwide have been swamped with complaints from victims, ranging from ordinary Malaysians to professionals such as doctors, engineers and lawyers. He described the surge in cases as a “national crime wave” that has devastated families and crushed hopes for a better future.
Lim stressed that leaving enforcement solely to the police or the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) was inadequate, as both agencies lacked the resources and expertise to tackle the scale of the problem.
“Banks are the vital intermediary enabling this digital fraud and theft to happen,” he said, adding that financial institutions should be required to suspend accounts showing suspicious large withdrawals.
Citing official figures, Lim noted that only RM6.7 million was recovered out of RM2.97 billion reported lost to scams in 2025 — a recovery rate he called “alarming and unacceptable”.
He said Bank Negara must lead a coordinated response involving all government departments to curb the surge in crime and protect the life savings of Malaysians.

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB rejects Anwar’s ‘rude, uncivilised’ claim, says exco acted within role
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 24 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim today rejected Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s description of his and the state executive council’s actions as “rude” and “uncivilised”, saying they had not made any decision to remove or appoint the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
Ismail said he respected Anwar’s concern for the Royal Institution but believed the Prime Minister’s criticism was based on an incomplete understanding of the actual role played by the Menteri Besar and the exco.
“I take note of the statement made by the honourable Prime Minister yesterday, who described my actions and those of the state executive council as rude and uncivilised.
“I respect the Prime Minister’s concern for the Royal Institution. However, I am concerned that the reprimand was based on an incomplete picture of the actual role of the Menteri Besar and the exco members,” he told a press conference at Klana Resort here.
Ismail, who is also the Juasseh assemblyman, said the state executive council had instead discussed the state administration’s position on a proclamation presented as the decision of the four Undangs.
“In this matter, the Menteri Besar and the exco did not make any decision to remove or appoint the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
“The state executive council discussed the state administration’s position on the proclamation presented as the decision of the four Undangs,” he said.
He said the exco’s agreement to subsequent administrative action did not mean that it had assumed the powers of the Undangs or made the decision on the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
“The state executive council’s agreement to the subsequent administrative action does not mean that the council took over the powers of the Undangs or became the party making the decision regarding the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar,” he said.
Ismail said he and the exco would not interfere in customary considerations or the selection process, which he said fell within the jurisdiction prescribed under the Constitution of the State of Negeri Sembilan 1959.
He said any questions regarding the validity of the proclamation, compliance with procedures and its constitutional effects should be determined according to the state constitution and relevant legal processes.
“We respect any court order that is in force,” he said.
Yesterday, Anwar criticised Ismail and the state executive council for attempting to remove Yang di Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, calling the move rude and uncivilised.
He said no state level authority has the mandate to question or alter the position of the Ruler.
Anwar stressed that the federal government is not interfering in the matter and said the issue of dethroning a Ruler is not straightforward.
He then said conflicting claims among the Undangs must be resolved before any decision can be considered valid.
Anwar added that any decision made by the properly appointed Undangs following the correct process would fall outside the jurisdiction of the federal government.

Title: Pensioner who endured seven years of golf balls hitting his home finally wins RM100,000 from Jitra resort
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — A 61-year-old government pensioner has been awarded RM100,000 in damages after enduring nearly seven years of stray golf balls pelting his bungalow in Bandar Darulaman, Jitra.
At the Alor Setar High Court, Judicial Commissioner Aimi Zaini Azhar ruled that golf course operator BDB Darulaman Golf & Resort Bhd and landowner BDB Land Sdn Bhd are jointly and severally liable for private nuisance,
FMT
reported.
“Operating a golf course is a lawful business, (but) it cannot be conducted in a manner that unreasonably infringes upon the basic safety and property rights of neighbouring homeowners,” the judge said in his judgment.
The court gave the defendants 60 days to heighten and extend safety netting near Hole 7, review tee markers and the line of play, install warning signs, and implement all measures necessary to stop golf balls from entering the property.
Plaintiff Nazli Ahmad Mahyadin moved into his home in December 2018, adjacent to Tee Box 7. Between August 2019 and January 2026, he lodged 16 police reports and repeated management complaints after errant shots shattered a glass window, cracked roof tiles, punctured his poultry coop, and dented exterior walls. Seven neighbours testified to experiencing similar intrusions.
Describing the evidence as overwhelming, the judge noted: “The invasion was not an isolated or passing inconvenience; it was a persistent, multi-year state of affairs,” adding that operating adjacent to a residential boundary carried an “obvious, foreseeable risk of off-target shots entering private yards”.
The court rejected Nazli’s claim for trespass because individual golfers rather than the defendants struck the balls, but held that private nuisance had been firmly established. Safety netting installed in 2020 and expanded in 2024 was ruled “reactive, delayed and demonstrably ineffective”.
BDB Land was also held liable despite arguing it was merely a landlord, with the court noting it was the operator's parent company, had participated in safety discussions, and had developed and sold the residential lots.
The court dismissed claims for special, exemplary, and aggravated damages, and ordered the defendants to pay RM20,000 in costs.

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB says exco barred from Wisma Negeri, urges review of directive
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 24 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim today said state executive councillors (exco) had been barred from entering their offices at Wisma Negeri and urged the relevant authorities to immediately review the directive.
Ismail, who is also the Juasseh assemblyman, said he had been informed that the exco members were not only prohibited from entering their respective offices, but were also prevented from carrying out their duties.
The palace had earlier announced that Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir revoked the exco appointments with immediate effect, citing breaches of their oath of office during a September 15 meeting.
“I have been informed that there is a restraining order or directive prohibiting the exco members from entering their respective offices.
“I have also been informed that it is not merely that they are not allowed to enter their exco offices at Wisma Negeri, but that they are also not allowed to carry out their duties as exco members,” he told a press conference at Klana Resort here.
Ismail said the directive was conveyed to the exco members verbally rather than in writing.
He urged the relevant authorities to review the directive, including its basis and scope, taking into account the ongoing dispute and the need to ensure that state administration and public affairs were not disrupted.
Ismail said the request was being made through proper channels and would not prevent the authorities from carrying out their security responsibilities.
“I urge all parties to give the state government and the legal process room to resolve this dispute.
“The state government will continue to act properly, respect the state’s Royal Institution and prioritise the interests of the people,” he said.
He also maintained that the existing exco members remained legitimate and should continue carrying out their duties as usual.
Ismail said this was important as preventing the exco members from entering their offices or holding exco meetings could affect decisions involving the interests of the people.
“If the exco members are not allowed to enter their offices or hold exco meetings and so on, this would effectively be a denial of the people’s rights because many of these decisions are related to the interests of the people,” he said.
Ismail also said he had never been consulted or advised regarding the termination of any exco member under Article 38(5) of the Constitution of the State of Negeri Sembilan 1959.
“Therefore, once again, I want to emphasise that the existing exco members remain legitimate and will continue to carry out their duties as usual,” he said.

Title: Batu Gajah council empowers community to tackle roaming livestock blamed for road accidents
Article:
BATU GAJAH, September 24 — The Batu Gajah District Council (MDBG) has become the first local authority in Malaysia to give communities legal power to rein in straying livestock — cattle, buffaloes and goats — animals that often wander into roads and pose serious danger to motorists.
MDBG secretary Muazatul Adawiyah Muhammad said the initiative allowed appointed community agents to act under the Local Government Act 1976 (Act 171) and the MDBG Licensing of Livestock and Stray Animals By-Laws 2012.
“This is a pilot project aimed at strengthening enforcement through the community, especially in areas where straying livestock have posed risks to public safety,” she told a press conference at the MDBG’s office here.
The initiative involves 16 representatives from the mukims of Tronoh, Lahat, Tanjung Tualang, Sungai Raya and Sungai Terap, who were appointed as MDBG Community Agents for Stray Animal Management.
Muazatul said their appointments would be for one year, from October 1 this year until September 30, 2027, in line with the JPKK appointment period.
“We see this as a pilot project and, if there are areas that need improvement, the appointments can be extended for another year,” she said.
She said the initiative received full approval from the Perak State Executive Council and was formalised through the presentation of appointment letters to the Village Development and Security Committee (JPKK) representatives.
Muazatul said the initiative began in July with the appointment and nomination process carried out in collaboration with the Kinta District and Land Office.
She said all appointed community agents were subsequently required to attend coordination meetings and intensive theoretical and practical training in August.
“The training was conducted with the cooperation of the Department of Veterinary Services and the Royal Malaysia Police, focusing on passive capture techniques without chasing the animals,” she said.
She said the approach was designed to comply with the Five Freedoms of Animal Welfare under the Animal Welfare Act 2015 (Act 772).
Muazatul added the agents, who have been delegated authority under By-law 112 of the relevant by-laws, underwent field operational tests at the end of August, with their work integrated with a live geotagging system to verify the location of each animal caught.
“The JPKK chairmen must be present with his team during their operation. Their role is to identify straying livestock, record their location through geotagging and immediately inform the relevant authorities.
“Once an animal is captured, they must also lodge a report with the police within 24 hours. The animal then will be transferred to MDBG’s seizure pound in Batu Gajah,” she said.
Muazatul said the geotagging system would improve transparency and prevent false claims.
She also warned livestock owners against allowing their animals to roam freely.
“Detained animals may be seized and their owners could be fined and charged management fees before release. Unclaimed animals may be auctioned to the public,” she added.
In order to avoid confusion, Muazatul said notices on the enforcement would be placed in all 16 localities to inform residents and livestock owners that the areas are supervised by the appointed community agents.
“Identification and uniforms for the agents may also be provided in future,”
Muazatul said the operating costs would be covered by fines and livestock auction proceeds.
“RM500 allowance for each animal caught would also be channelled to the JPKK or relevant association’s official account to fund community activities,” she said.

Title: Cheras landslide displaces 80 residents; families wait on safety verdict before returning home
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — The duration of the evacuation for residents affected by the landslide at Block D of Damai Perdana Apartments in Bandar Damai Perdana, Cheras, will depend on a technical assessment of the building’s structural safety.
Kajang Municipal Council (MPKj) Councillor for Zone 6 Tan Kah Hoe said observations and assessments by the relevant agencies, which began yesterday, continued today, with the full technical report expected to be ready within the next few days.
The agencies involved include the Public Works Department (JKR), Department of Irrigation and Drainage (JPS), Minerals and Geoscience Department (JMG) and MPKj.
“I have asked the agencies to complete the report as soon as possible. They said it would take a few days,” he told Bernama when contacted here today.
On the water supply disruption affecting the four-block apartment complex, which comprises 360 residential units, Tan said water supply had been restored to Blocks A and B this morning.
“Block D remains without water supply, while restoring the supply to Block C is taking a little longer as the relevant authorities are identifying the route of the affected pipeline,” he said.
On the affected residents, Tan said 15 local families were currently staying at the temporary relief centre (PPS) at the Desa Baiduri community hall as of yesterday, compared with four families initially.
“For now, accommodation and food for the affected residents are being managed by the Social Welfare Department.
“Police are also assisting with security at the affected homes to ensure the area remains safe,” he said.
On Tuesday, about 80 residents from 45 units at Block D were ordered to evacuate immediately following a landslide on the hillside near the block at about 8pm, believed to have been caused by an underground water leak. — Bernama

Title: ‘Many flowers make spring’: Anwar affirms Malaysia open to China’s digital investment
Article:
HANGZHOU, Sept 24 — Malaysia will continue to be open to China’s investment in digital technology as well as cooperation, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Speaking at the 5th Global Digital Trade Expo (GDTE) opening ceremony here Thursday, Anwar credited the Chinese government’s willingness to showcase and share technologies through various platforms.
“From food to new technology, and the host China, as you host digitally today, has shown your willingness to showcase and share this technology. This applies well to the digital economy and (this is) why we will continue to open our economy to benefit digital investments and partnerships.
“Thank you for allowing us to showcase Malaysia’s national pavilion, including Chinese participation,” he said.
At the same time, the prime minister also shared Malaysia’s advantages, which are the discipline of their workers, skill, multilingual workforce, rules-based economy, and a base for reaching markets across Asia and beyond.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, welcomed China’s President Xi Jinping’s strong position that digital trade and artificial intelligence (AI) should help mitigate inequality instead of worsening it.
Citing a Chinese proverb, “a single flower alone does not make spring; when many flowers blossom, spring fills the garden”, the prime minister said progress will mean little if its gains are confined to a few countries, a few companies, a few communities or elites.
“A stronger digital economy will be one in which more nations can take part, more businesses can compete, and more people can prosper. Let us work together to help build this economy,” Anwar emphasised.
Held at the Hangzhou Grand Convention and Exhibition Centre, the five-day expo, officiated by Premier Li Qiang, is one of China’s major digital economy platforms that highlights AI and global cooperation.
Anwar is in China for a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou, which ends today. The working visit includes a high-level bilateral meeting with Li and engagements with Chinese leaders and captains of industry. — Bernama

Title: EC says 17 new Sarawak seats unlikely ready for next state election
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 24 — The 17 proposed new Sarawak state seats are unlikely to be in place for the next state election, Election Commission (EC) chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said.
He said the review of the electoral boundaries for the seats would take longer than February 2027, when the term of the Sarawak government expires.
“The term of the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly expires in February 2027, so based on the process we need to go through, I expect we will not be able to use the new seats in the next state election,” he told reporters after visiting the exhibition venue for the proposed Sarawak Electoral Boundary Review at the Kuching North City Hall (DBKU) here today.
In July, the Sarawak Legislative Assembly passed the State Legislative Assembly (Composition of Members) Bill 2025 to add 17 new seats, bringing the total number of seats from 82 to 99.
Meanwhile, Ramlan said the EC had received 18 objections to the proposed Sarawak Electoral Boundary Review so far, involving various issues including changes to polling district centres.
“There were also several objections concerning the names of certain state constituencies in Sarikei, Bintulu and Sibu. We will assess and examine these matters in greater detail later,” he said. — Bernama

Title: ‘Govern AI or it will govern us,’ Anwar warns in China
Article:
HANGZHOU, Sept 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called for an ethics-driven approach to artificial intelligence (AI) and a more open, rules-based digital trade regime to ensure developing nations share in the gains of technological progress.
Speaking at the opening ceremony of the 5th Global Digital Trade Expo here, he acknowledged China’s advancement in visualisation and AI as well as its role in sharing technological advancements with the Global South.
“To my mind, this is what is remarkable about the Chinese leadership, and their willingness to continue to give meaning and essence to real globalisation,” he said in his keynote address here.
Held at the Hangzhou Grand Convention and Exhibition Centre, the five-day expo officiated by China’s Premier Li Qiang is one of China’s major digital economy platforms.
Anwar, who is also the finance ninister, said Malaysia’s objectives in AI are clear, namely to raise productivity, help smaller firms compete, and move industries into higher-value work, while ensuring that Malaysians gain from technological change rather than merely live with its consequences.
“The principle remains, either we govern artificial intelligence or artificial intelligence will govern us,” he said, while calling for an ethics-based framework to ensure that innovation and technological advancement remain firmly in the service of humanity
He said this was a fundamental issue that touched on the recurring problem of the digital divide, particularly as nations pursued rapid technological advancement amid persistent socio-economic inequalities.
“Exponential growth of AI, for example, may be what most nations aspire to, but what purpose would it really serve humanity if such expansion only leads to widening the gap between wealthy and developing nations, advanced and developing economies?
“This is not an imagined or exaggerated fear but a profound concern for the well-being of regions, nations, and communities. The question is whether these technologies will give developing countries a larger say in their own future or leave them dependent on technologies designed elsewhere,” he said.
Anwar said true economic advancement could not proceed in a vacuum, while real expansion of technology could not be sustained without considering the technology gap.
The Prime Minister’s three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou concludes today.
China has remained Malaysia’s largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, with total bilateral trade reaching US$113.82 billion (RM456.68 billion) between January and August this year. — Bernama

Title: Home minister: Police probing Negeri Sembilan royal dispute from ‘every angle’
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — Police are investigating the escalating royal dispute in Negeri Sembilan from all angles following multiple police reports lodged on the matter, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said.
Saifuddin said that while operational details remain confidential, security forces are strictly focused on preserving public order, averting street confrontations, and safeguarding the public,
NST
reported.
“The police have taken preventive security measures to ensure no gatherings could lead to confrontations.
“They are looking at every angle,” he said
Saifuddin affirmed that he is leaving it entirely to the police to complete their probe before determining whether to submit the investigation papers to the Attorney General’s Chambers for further instruction.
Addressing Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s position on purported moves to unseat the Negeri Sembilan Ruler, Saifuddin noted that the prime minister views any attempt to depose a hereditary sovereign as a matter of utmost gravity under Malaysia’s constitutional monarchy.
The unfolding controversy has sparked a series of claims and counter-claims surrounding the standing and authority of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.

Title: Former Tabung Haji COO Adi Azuan charged with receiving RM302,000 in house renovations
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 24 — Former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chief operating officer Datuk Adi Azuan Abdul Ghani pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to three counts of graft involving over RM302,000 in home renovation works.
Adi Azuan, 56, claimed trial to all charges after they were read out before Sessions Court Judge Awang Kerisnada Awang Mahmud,
The Star
reported.
According to the charge sheets, Adi Azuan, in his capacity as TH chief operating officer, allegedly accepted gratification for himself in the form of renovation expenses amounting to RM235,866.58, RM50,698.74, and RM15,933.95 for three residential properties at different locations.
He is accused of receiving the works from AG Reka Sdn Bhd director Thamsulazri Ismail, an individual whom the accused knew had official connections with his public duties at the pilgrimage fund.
The offences were allegedly committed on March 7, 2017, at the three properties located in Shah Alam, Kota Damansara, and USJ 2, Subang Jaya.
The charges were framed under Section 165 of the Penal Code, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of two years, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Muaz Ahmad Khairuddin informed the court that the offences were non-bailable, but proposed bail at RM70,000 with one surety should the court exercise its discretion to grant temporary release.
“We leave it to the court’s discretion if it decides to impose additional bail conditions,” Muaz said.
In mitigation, defence counsel Wan Azwan Aiman Wan Fakhruddin appealed for a lower bail sum of RM30,000, stating that his client is the sole provider for four sons aged between 12 and 25 who are still studying, including his eldest who is currently in university. The lawyer also requested that the court not impound Adi Azuan’s passport, contending that he poses no flight risk.
Awang Kerisnada fixed bail at RM50,000 with two sureties and ordered the accused to surrender his passport to the custody of the court.
“If he needs to use his passport, he can write to the court,” Awang Kerisnada said.
The court scheduled the case for mention on Nov 25.
Adi Azuan was originally slated to be charged on Sept 3, but the proceedings were adjourned after he was admitted to hospital to undergo an angiogram procedure.

Title: JPJ denies fake news on Rohingya driving licences, files MCMC report
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 24 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) today denied a statement published on the ‘Along Auto Parts’ Facebook account, titled “JPJ Proposes Allowing Rohingyas to Obtain Driving Licenses?” which was allegedly posted in the form of an official news report.
Consequently, JPJ has lodged a report with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) to enable an investigation and appropriate action regarding the dissemination of the content.
“JPJ takes a serious view of any party producing, modifying, or disseminating content that uses the department’s name, identity, or image in a way that could mislead the public and undermine JPJ’s credibility,” the department said in a Facebook post today.
The public is advised not to spread information of unverified authenticity and to always refer to official JPJ channels for accurate and verified information.
A check of the ‘Along Auto Parts’ Facebook page revealed that the post, uploaded 12 hours ago, had not yet been deleted as of 9:15 am today, garnering over 1,800 comments and 325 shares. — Bernama

Title: AGC appeals High Court acquittal of teen in Bandar Utama schoolmate murder case
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) has filed an appeal against a High Court decision that acquitted and discharged a 15-year-old boy of murdering a schoolmate at a secondary school in Petaling Jaya last year.
In a statement today, the AGC confirmed that it filed a Notice of Appeal at the Court of Appeal on September 22, seeking to overturn the Shah Alam High Court’s September 14 ruling that freed the teenager of the murder charge under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
The statement did not specificy the case, but the material information indicates it is the matter being contested.
The High Court, presided over by Judge Adlin Abdul Majid, acquitted the boy at the close of the defence case after finding that he was of unsound mind at the time of the offence, an outcome the AGC is now contesting before the appellate court.
The case arose from the fatal stabbing of a 16-year-old female student in a school toilet between 9.20am and 9.35am on October 14, 2025.
The accused, who was 14 at the time of the incident, was charged under Section 302, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years, though Malaysian law bars capital punishment for juvenile offenders under the age of 18.
During the trial, the defence invoked Section 84 of the Penal Code, successfully entering the "unsoundness of mind" defence.
Following the acquittal, Adlin ordered the teenager to be admitted to Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta in Perak for psychiatric care at the pleasure of the Sultan of Selangor, pursuant to provisions under Section 97 of the Child Act 2001.
A total of 11 prosecution witnesses and two defence witnesses, including the accused, testified during the trial, which was conducted in camera due to the defendant's status as a minor.

Title: Azalina: Anti‑Bullying Tribunal resolves five cases with awards, 55 complaints lodged since launch
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The Anti-Bullying Tribunal (TAB) has received 55 complaints, with five cases decided through awards as of Tuesday, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
She said the awards included apologies to victims, participation in a counselling programme and RM2,000 in compensation in one case.
“This reflects TAB’s approach, which is not solely focused on punishment, but also emphasises victim recovery and correcting the perpetrator’s behaviour,” she said in a statement today.
Azalina said that, beyond the legal framework, efforts to address bullying also depended on society’s willingness to speak up and take action.
She said victims should come forward to seek help, while those who witness bullying should also have the courage to speak up, as bullying is not a joke and must not be normalised under any circumstances.
Meanwhile, she said that, in line with the Madani Government’s commitment to addressing bullying seriously and comprehensively, she launched the Anti-Bullying Act 2026 (Act 876) Literacy Programme and the Role of TAB at the Royal Military College (RMC), Sungai Besi, today.
The programme is part of the government’s efforts to enhance public understanding, particularly among the younger generation, of the protection available under Act 876 and the functions and role of TAB, including the procedure for lodging complaints, the hearing process and the remedies available to victims. — Bernama

Title: Woman killed, husband and four children injured in Tanah Merah head‑on collision
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 24 — A woman was killed while her husband and four children were injured in an accident involving their Perodua Alza and a Toyota Hilux at Jalan Rantau Panjang-Panglima Bayu, Tanah Merah, yesterday.
Tanah Merah district police chief Supt Mohd Haki Hasbullah said Tengku Ziarulwida Tuan Zainudin, 39, who was a passenger in the Perodua Alza, was killed on the spot in the 3pm incident.
He said preliminary investigations showed that the Perodua Alza, driven by Tengku Ziarulwida’s husband, Mohd Saifulzawawi Ghani, 39, collided head-on with the Toyota Hilux.
The family was travelling from Rantau Panjang, Pasir Mas, towards Panglima Bayu.
“Mohd Saifulzawawi and two of his children were seriously injured and admitted to the Red Zone of Tanah Merah Hospital. The other two children are in the Yellow Zone,” he said in a statement last night.
The Toyota Hilux driver, Che Ibrahim Che Min, 48, sustained minor injuries.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. — Bernama

Title: Private hospitals urge government to boost MMC and healthcare watchdog in Budget 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 24 — The Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM) has urged the government to increase federal funding for the Malaysian Medical Council (MMC), warning that persistent underinvestment in the medical regulator threatens to weaken oversight and undermine public trust in the healthcare system.
In a press statement today, APHM president Datuk Dr Kuljit Singh said budgetary allocations must be enhanced for the MMC, the statutory body responsible for regulating medical practitioners and upholding professional ethics, alongside the Malaysia Healthcare Travel Council (MHTC).
A third critical body, the Malaysian Society for Quality in Health (MSQH), which oversees nationwide hospital accreditation and quality audits, currently receives no direct government funding at all.
“Sustained underinvestment in these institutions risks weakening oversight, compromising quality assurance processes, and eroding the standards that patients and the public depend on,” the statement said.
The appeal arrives just over two weeks before Budget 2027 is tabled in Parliament on October 9.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan previously indicated that the upcoming national budget will emphasise raising the nation’s “social floor” and strengthening institutional governance alongside economic growth priorities.
APHM said the call was as an urgent patient-safety agenda rather than a routine administrative appeal.
The MMC’s core functions, which include licensing doctors, enforcing professional conduct, and adjudicating disciplinary inquiries, form the bedrock of patient confidence in medical competency and accountability.
The association argued that a resource-constrained regulator faces the risk of protracted disciplinary timelines, weaker compliance enforcement, and diminished operational bandwidth to keep pace with a rapidly expanding healthcare sector.
Dr Kuljit also linked the funding shortfall to the wider medical tourism economy, contending that an industry generating significant national revenue must reinvest in the regulatory ecosystem that guarantees its global reputation.
He highlighted the healthcare travel sector as a “consistent and growing contributor to national revenue,” arguing that economic value generated by the industry should help sustain the regulatory and accreditation institutions that establish Malaysia’s clinical credibility abroad.
“Ensuring adequate funding for these bodies is a necessary investment in patient safety, professional accountability, and public trust,” the statement said, cautioning that without adequate financial backing, the ability to “maintain rigorous standards, enforce governance, and continuously improve care delivery will be significantly constrained.”
APHM added that it “stands ready to work collaboratively with the Ministry of Health and relevant stakeholders” to establish sustainable financial support for the three institutions.

Title: Woman found dead in Kuala Kangsar home, police arrest two suspects believed to be relatives
Article:
IPOH, Sept 24 — A woman was found dead in a pool of blood in the living room of a house in Kampung Cheh Kati, Kuala Kangsar yesterday.
Kuala Kangsar police chief ACP Heisham Harun said a report was lodged at 2.38pm after the victim’s family found her lying face down and unconscious inside the house.
He said police subsequently arrested two men believed to be related to the victim and suspected to be linked to the case.
“Initial investigations found that the incident was believed to have stemmed from a misunderstanding between the victim and the suspects.
“Police also found a knife believed to have been used as the weapon,” he said in a statement last night.
Heisham said the victim’s body was sent to the Taiping Hospital Forensic Department for a post-mortem, adding that the two suspects would be brought to court tomorrow for a remand application.
Members of the public with information on the case are urged to contact ASP Mohamad Fadhil Ab Wahab from the Kuala Kangsar District Police Headquarters Criminal Investigation Division at 019-7272033 or the Kuala Kangsar IPD Operations Room at 05-7762222.

Title: PM Anwar says Malaysia manages disputes with neighbours through dialogue, not distrust
Article:
HANGZHOU, Sept 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia manages disagreements with all neighbouring nations through continuous diplomatic engagement and constructive dialogue, rather than conflict or distrust.
In a wide-ranging address highlighting the deep cultural and diplomatic ties between Malaysia and China, Anwar shared personal anecdotes of mutual respect and philosophical kinship with Chinese leadership.
He praised Chinese President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang for treating smaller nations with humility and as equal partners, a quality he noted as vital for developing countries navigating post-colonial realities and modern geopolitical pressures.
“People always ask me, why do you seem so close to China? I ask in return, what kind of question is that? We are close to China because China is our neighbour.
“I find it difficult to understand the attitude that promotes the view that ‘China cannot be trusted’. Such an attitude stems from certain other prejudices, but it certainly does not represent us,” said Anwar during the global launch of the Chinese edition of his latest book,
Rethinking Ourselves: Justice, Reform, and Ignorance in Postnormal Times
, here today.
Also present at the launch were Transport Minister Anthony Loke, Investment, Trade and Industry Minister, Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution.
The book focuses on how identity can be reshaped and pathways toward coexistence can be pursued against the backdrop of the rise of newly independent nations and their struggles against colonialism and imperialism.
It advocates shifting the focus toward “shared prosperity,” rather than pursuing self-interest alone.
Published by World Affairs Press under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China, the book was translated by Dr Yan Lijin.
About 5,000 copies have been printed.
The original English version of
Rethinking Ourselves: Justice, Reform, and Ignorance in Postnormal Times
was published in October 2025 by Penguin Random House SEA.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, is currently in China for a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou, that includes high-level bilateral meeting with Li and engagements with Chinese leaders and captains of industry. — Bernama
